name: Get email template
description: Call this when you have a template id and need that template's full stored definition — its name, category, published state, thumbnail URL, and the complete drag-and-drop content tree — for example before rendering it in the editor or copying its structure. The id must already be known; this action does not search or list, so use the editor template-listing action to find candidate ids first, and use the campaign actions when you need the content of a saved campaign rather than a reusable template.
preconditions: A template with the given id must exist and be visible to the authenticated account.
The caller must be an authenticated Brevo web-app session with access to the account that owns the template.

id.description: Identifier of the template to retrieve, taken from the request path. Observed as a 24-character hexadecimal object id, e.g. "5ea1551d2e9ad34b8640be9f".
Identifier of the template, matching the requested id.

EntityType.description: Kind of content this template defines. Observed value: "email".

publisherNewsletterId.description: Numeric id of the underlying newsletter/template record in the publisher system.

publisherAccountId.description: Numeric id of the Brevo account the template belongs to.

category.description: Grouping label used by the template gallery. Observed value: "Layout".

published.description: Whether the template is published and therefore selectable in the editor.

thumbnailUrl.description: Absolute URL of the generated preview image for the template.

order.description: Sort weight used to position the template within its category.

content.description: The editor's structured template definition: the document tree of rows, columns and blocks plus authoring metadata. Rendered HTML fragments inside it may contain template placeholders such as {{ mirror }} and {{ label.template.footer.view_in_browser }}.

author.description: Author metadata stored with the template; observed empty.

body.description: Root node of the template document, whose nested "content" arrays hold the rows, columns and content blocks of the design.
